correctness.rationale: Specializing the cited L-ADMM update gives the frozen scalar recurrence, and the exact w-optimality relation forces \(y_{k+1}=mw_{k+1}\) after one update. The resulting 2-by-2 matrix has the stated trace and determinant. The discriminant and root-derivative sign calculation correctly yields critical damping for \(r<1\), the full \(r=1\) plateau, trace-zero balancing for \(1<r<\phi\), and the \(h=0\) boundary for \(r\ge\phi\). An independent dense numerical minimization over representative values on both sides of every transition reproduced the closed-form minimizers.
risks: The theorem optimizes asymptotic spectral radius only; repeated-root finite-time norms can have polynomial prefactors.
The \(h<1\) branches are instance-specific and are not claimed to satisfy the source paper’s general sufficient majorization condition.

value.rationale: The symmetric scalar quadratic is the natural single-mode test for separating penalty and linearization stabilization. The exact optimum has three distinct mechanisms plus a nontrivial golden-ratio boundary and an entire balanced-penalty plateau, showing exactly when the general majorization choice is conservative. These are useful sharp modal benchmarks rather than a routine restatement of convergence.
risks: No claim is made that one scalar optimum jointly optimizes a multi-eigenvalue or nonsymmetric problem.

limitations: Symmetric scalar quadratic, constant stabilization, fixed penalty, and asymptotic spectral radius only.
